title: Cyclone Murasu Makes Landfall in Andhra Pradesh as Odisha Evacuates 1.6 Lakh People
excerpt: The severe storm began crossing the Andhra coast at 1 a.m. on Tuesday, the second cyclone to hit the region in a week. Odisha plans to move 3.33 lakh people to 1,139 shelters.
body:
• Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu began making landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast at 1:00 a.m. local time on Tuesday, the India Meteorological Department said via Reuters.
  • It is the second storm to hit the region in a week: Cyclone Arnab, which made landfall last Wednesday, killed at least six people.
  • Odisha has moved more than 1.60 lakh people to safety, including 1.50 lakh in Ganjam district alone, with plans to evacuate 3.33 lakh people to 1,139 shelters.
  • At least 19 flights were cancelled across Andhra Pradesh on Monday, and more than 300 rescue teams are deployed in Odisha; check your flight status with your airline if you are travelling to or from Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam, Tirupati or Chennai.

Cyclone Murasu began making landfall along India's eastern coast early on Tuesday, the country's weather department said, the second storm to hit the region in a week as authorities evacuated thousands of people to safety, Reuters reported. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the severe cyclonic storm started making landfall at 1:00 a.m. local time (1930 GMT) over the coast of Andhra Pradesh.

Authorities in Andhra Pradesh began evacuating people on Monday and planned to move some 30,000 to safety in the state, which is in the path of the cyclone, Reuters reported. IMD forecasts said Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu to its south would be worst hit.

The Odisha evacuation

The larger evacuation ran in neighbouring Odisha. The state government on Monday moved over 1.60 lakh people to safety, including 1.50 lakh in Ganjam district alone, with plans to evacuate a total of 3.33 lakh people to 1,139 prepared shelters, according to Jagran English, citing Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari. Eight districts were named as high-risk: Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput, Rayagada, Malkangiri, Kandhamal, Kalahandi and Puri.

More than 300 rescue teams from the NDRF, Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force and Odisha Fire Service are deployed, with nodal officers in every village, the report said. Nearly 150 landslide-prone areas have been identified in Gajapati district after a week of rain. Schools and anganwadi centres in affected southern districts are closed on Tuesday, with closures in Malkangiri and Kandhamal extending to Wednesday.

Track, winds and travel disruption

Murasu — the name means war drum — was expected to cross between Nellore and Narasapur, south of Ongole, late on Monday night into early Tuesday, with wind speeds of 100-110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph, according to Jagran English. IMD Director PLN Murthy told IANS the storm lay over the west-central Bay of Bengal, about 80 kilometres east of Nellore.

The storm forced the cancellation of at least 19 domestic flights across Andhra Pradesh on Monday — 12 at Vijayawada, three at Visakhapatnam and two at Tirupati, with further cancellations at Chennai — and passengers were advised to verify flight status directly with their airlines. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu reviewed preparedness with district officials and directed that preventing loss of life be the top priority, the report said.

A second blow in a week

Murasu formed over the Bay of Bengal days after Cyclone Arnab, classified by the IMD as a very severe cyclonic storm, made landfall in Andhra Pradesh last Wednesday and killed at least six people, Reuters reported. In Odisha, Arnab had already affected 1.18 lakh people and damaged nearly 90,000 hectares of standing crops, and farmers in Ganjam warned that fresh flooding would rot standing paddy, according to Jagran English. Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has announced a special relief package for people affected by Arnab, to be reviewed after Murasu's damage is assessed.

Extremely heavy rainfall was forecast for parts of coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema through Tuesday, easing over November 4-5. Follow live updates via Jagran English's Murasu tracker coverage and district administration notices if you have family in the affected districts.
